Title: Verify that measurement cloth photo URLs cannot be accessed by unauthorized users via direct URL manipulation
Section: Order Management - Insecure Direct Object Reference
Preconditions: Two users exist: User A (owner of an order with a measurement cloth photo) and User B (unauthorized to view User A's order). Both users are authenticated.
Steps:
1. Log in as User A and navigate to the order details screen for an order with a measurement cloth photo.
2. Copy the measurement cloth photo URL from the response or UI.
3. Log out and log in as User B.
4. Paste the copied URL into a browser or API client and attempt to access it.
5. Repeat steps 1-4 for an unauthenticated session (no login).

Test Data: Use an order ID owned by User A (e.g., Order ID: ORD-2023-001).
Expected Result: User B and unauthenticated sessions receive HTTP 403 (Forbidden) or 404 (Not Found) when attempting to access the measurement cloth photo URL. User A can access the URL successfully.

Title: Verify that malformed or path-traversal sequences in measurement cloth photo URLs are rejected during order retrieval
Preconditions: User has an existing order with a measurement cloth photo. User is authenticated and authorized to view the order.
Steps:
1. Log in to the application as a user with access to the order.
2. Use a proxy tool (e.g., Burp Suite) to intercept the request to the order details endpoint.
3. Modify the measurement cloth photo URL in the request to include path traversal sequences (e.g., '../../', '..%2F', or null bytes).
4. Forward the modified request and observe the response.
5. Repeat for other malformed URLs (e.g., overly long strings, invalid characters).

Test Data: Use an order ID known to have a measurement cloth photo (e.g., Order ID: ORD-2023-001). Modify the URL to include '../../malicious.jpg' or '..%2Fmalicious.jpg'.
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP 400 (Bad Request) or 403 (Forbidden) and a generic error message (e.g., 'Invalid image URL'). The response does not expose internal system details or allow access to unauthorized files.
